guide.a.fields_support_formatting: Listing descriptions, terms and conditions, homepage text, and contact page text all understand Markdown — a simple way of marking text as bold, italic, or linked, using ordinary characters.
guide.a.what_formatting_can_i_use: Bold with **bold**, italic with *italic*, links with [text](https://...), and lists with - at the start of a line. See the Markdown cheat sheet for more options.
guide.q.how_does_the_visual_editor_work: How does the visual editor work?
guide.a.how_does_the_visual_editor_work:
Markdown fields open in a visual editor — you style text with buttons instead of typing the marks. The toolbar covers bold, italic, links, headings, bulleted and numbered lists, and quotes. You can also use Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I, or type the marks directly — - starts a list, # a heading, > a quote, and [text](url) becomes a link — and they convert as you type.

Everything is stored as plain Markdown underneath. Click Edit markdown under the field to work on the raw marks (useful for anything the toolbar does not cover), and Edit visually to switch back. A field whose existing text uses formatting the visual editor cannot keep (tables, for example) opens as raw Markdown, so nothing is quietly rewritten behind your back.
guide.q.insert_image_in_text: How do I put an image in the text?
guide.a.insert_image_in_text:
Click Image in the visual editor's toolbar. A window opens over the page with the pictures in your image library. Click one to put it where your cursor is.

To add a new picture, fill in Upload a new image in the same window and click Upload image. The picture goes into the library and into your text.

To close the window without a picture, click the close icon or press Escape. You cannot close it while a picture uploads.

In the raw Markdown, a picture shows as ![name](img#12). The Image button only shows when image storage is set up.
guide.q.preview_text_in_a_window: How do I preview my text?
guide.a.preview_text_in_a_window:
Click Preview under a formatting box. The preview opens in a window over the page. The page stays usable while the window is open.

Only the part that you are working in is bright. The rest is dim. When you click the page, the page turns bright and the windows turn dim. The windows stay open. Click a window to make it bright again.

To move the window, drag its title bar. To make it smaller, click the minus icon. The window keeps only its title bar. Click the title bar to open it again. To close the window, click the close icon.

You can open more than one preview. The window you used last stays on top.

On a phone, the window fills the screen. You can still make it smaller or close it. You cannot drag it.

If you leave the page while a window is open, your browser asks you to confirm.
